name: FlyHead
summary: A testbed for connectome-driven control that connects a simulated whole-brain fruit-fly connectome (FlyWire) to a real wheel-legged robot. The LIF brain model is taken unmodified from eonsystemspbc/fly-brain; as sole developer, built everything around it: sensor encoders, the descending-neuron decoder, GPU acceleration, the safety layer, LiDAR SLAM navigation, a web console and a 3D site, demonstrated on the real robot.

name: code-with-pi
summary: A terminal broker that lets an AI coding agent and its user monitor or take over the same live shell. Written in C11 for Windows and Linux.

name: ANSYS_skill
summary: A checker for automated ANSYS Mechanical workflows that records which stage a run reached and the result evidence behind it.

name: ForgeSpec-Studio
summary: A design automation tool that converts a loose engineering brief into a reviewable assembly specification and deterministic CadQuery source.

name: ANSYS_simulation_IOP
summary: Finite-element models and analysis scripts for studying transpalpebral eye-pressure measurement, built in ANSYS APDL and released as research code.

name: Harmony_TaskFlow
summary: A HarmonyOS systems-integration experiment: a task app with calendar sign-in, a cloud back end and a native proxy core.

name: CoughKD
summary: A research pipeline for cough-audio screening. It prepares subject-disjoint data and distils large audio teachers into smaller student models.

name: pixel_probetop
summary: A lightweight multi-server monitor used to watch the research group's GPU servers, with a web UI and an Android viewer.

name: stm32-cli-toolkit
summary: A set of shell wrappers around OpenOCD for building and flashing STM32 projects from a terminal or headless machine.

name: MES204 LCD projects
summary: STM32F446 character-LCD projects from the Microprocessor Systems module, including a T-Rex game, custom characters and graphics experiments.

name: terminal-gauss-Mamma-viz
summary: A terminal renderer written in C that draws mathematical surfaces in perspective using ANSI colour.

name: sky_monitor_api
summary: An astronomy API built with FastAPI that returns the stars, planets and deep-sky objects visible from a given location and time, with a live web demo.
